original_question: For the Einstein-Vlasov and related collisionless matter models, prove global existence of classical spatially inhomogeneous solutions for small initial data, and prove existence and uniqueness for general spatially homogeneous solutions such as Bianchi type IX while also analyzing the large-data regime.
target_in_paper: Problem P4 in §3.3 ("Yang–Mills equations and GR"), p. 29: "Prove the global existence of classical spatially inhomogeneous solutions for small initial data in collisionless matter models. Prove an existence and uniqueness theorem for general spatially homogeneous (such as Bianchi type IX) solutions of the Einstein-Vlasov equations and investigate the large initial data case."
correct_elements: Your draft is already very close to the paper’s actual formulation. It correctly captures all three components of Problem P4: (i) global existence of classical spatially inhomogeneous solutions for small initial data, (ii) existence and uniqueness for general spatially homogeneous solutions, with Bianchi type IX singled out as an example, and (iii) the need to address the large-initial-data regime. It also correctly identifies the Einstein-Vlasov/collisionless-matter setting.
missing_details: The paper places the problem specifically in general relativity, in the setting of self-gravitating collisionless matter models.
The first clause is stated for collisionless matter models in general, whereas the second clause is stated specifically for the Einstein-Vlasov equations.
Bianchi type IX is only an example of the intended class of general spatially homogeneous solutions, not the whole scope of the homogeneous part.

The survey formulation does not specify the function spaces, differentiability class beyond 'classical', asymptotic conditions, spacetime dimension, or a norm defining 'small' versus 'large' initial data; a stand-alone restatement should preserve that this is intentionally left open in the paper.

The nearby context emphasizes that many GR analogues are known only in special symmetric settings, for weak solutions, near equilibrium, or in selected model classes; the open problem is the general analytical case.
refined_question: In general relativity, for self-gravitating collisionless matter models, prove global existence of classical spatially inhomogeneous solutions for sufficiently small initial data; and, for the Einstein-Vlasov system, prove an existence-and-uniqueness theorem for general spatially homogeneous solutions—including, as a representative case, Bianchi type IX—and investigate the large-initial-data case.
justification: The draft is essentially a paraphrase of the paper’s official open problem P4, and no narrower or more precise equivalent theorem/conjecture is given elsewhere in the paper. The immediately preceding paragraph identifies the intended scope as self-gravitating collisionless matter models in GR, recalls known Newtonian results (Vlasov-Poisson and Boltzmann) and partial GR analogues, and then states P4 verbatim. So the paper-faithful refinement is to keep the wording very close to P4 while making explicit the GR/self-gravitating context and the distinction between the broader collisionless-matter clause and the specifically Einstein-Vlasov homogeneous clause.
